facts.statement: Arkansaurus lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: Arkansaurus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: in what is now North America

facts.statement: The original bones were donated by Joe B. Friday and now reside at the University of Arkansas Museum Collections.
facts.quote: The original bones, donated to the university by Friday, currently reside at the University of Arkansas Museum Collections

facts.statement: The full species name Arkansaurus fridayi was first published by Angela K. Braden in 1998.
facts.quote: The full species name was first published by Angela K. Braden in 1998

facts.statement: Arkansaurus measured about 4.6 meters long and weighed about 380.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Arkansaurus measured about 4.6 m long and weighed about 380.5 kg

facts.statement: Arkansaurus had strongly curved foot claws, which was an exception among most ornithomimosaurians that typically had flat claws.
facts.quote: with the strong curvature of the foot claws being the only exception: most ornithomimosaurians had flat claws

facts.statement: The holotype foot revealed a greenstick fracture, the first such record among dinosaur fossils, and evidence of a potential gout.
facts.quote: The holotype also revealed a greenstick fracture, which is the first record among dinosaur fossils, and a potential gout

facts.statement: Arkansaurus is classified in the Ornithomimosauria in a basal position, outside of the Ornithomimidae family.
facts.quote: Arkansaurus was placed in the Ornithomimosauria in a basal position, outside of the Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: Arkansaurus was likely a fast-moving omnivore between 1.8 and 4.6 meters long.
facts.quote: Arkansaurus fue probablemente un omnívoro de movimiento rápido entre 1,8 y 4.6 metros de largo

facts.statement: Arkansaurus likely had long arms ending in three hands with claws on the fingers.
facts.quote: Sus largos brazos probablemente habrían terminado en tres manos con garras en los dedos

facts.statement: The foot claws of Arkansaurus were strongly bent downwards.
facts.quote: Las garras del pie están fuertemente dobladas hacia abajo

facts.statement: It is debated whether Arkansaurus lost its first toe or if the absence is due to fossilization processes.
facts.quote: Una posible diferencia es que Arkansaurus parece perder el primer dedo del pie, aunque también puede ser el resultado de la posibilidad de perderse durante la fosilización

facts.statement: Arkansaurus fossils were first noticed by Joe B. Friday in August 1972 when he saw vultures circling his land in Locksburg, Arkansas.
facts.quote: En agosto de 1972, Joe B. Friday, que era dueño de una estación de servicio en Locksburg, Arkansas, notó algunos buitres dando vueltas sobre su tierra.

facts.statement: Friday collected the bones and displayed them at his gas station for several months before they were recognized as dinosaur remains.
facts.quote: Los junto y durante algunos meses mostró los fósiles en su estación.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Dr. James H. Quinn identified the bones as dinosaur fossils and prepared them for study.
facts.quote: Quinn reconoció los restos fosilizados como dinosaurios y preparó los huesos.

facts.statement: The known fossil record of Arkansaurus consists of three metatarsals, four phalanges, and three claws.
facts.quote: En total, se encontraron tres metatarsianos, cuatro falanges y tres garras de Arkansaurus se conocen.

facts.statement: The full species name Arkansaurus fridayi was formally published in 1998 by Angela K. Braden, noting that James H. Quinn had used the name informally earlier.
facts.quote: El nombre completo de la especie fue publicado por primera vez por Angela K. Braden en 1998, mencionando que Quinn había usado informalmente la combinación "Arkansaurus fridayi".

facts.statement: Daniel Chure initially promised to name the fossils but was unable to do so at that time.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo asociado Daniel Chure prometió nombrar los fósiles después de todo, pero no pudo encontrar tiempo para esto.

facts.statement: Arkansaurus was officially designated as the state dinosaur of Arkansas in 2017.
facts.quote: "Arkansaurus" fue declarado el dinosaurio oficial del estado de Arkansas en 2017.

facts.statement: Arkansaurus was discovered in Lockesburg, Arkansas, and is classified as a bipedal ornithomimosaurian dinosaur.
facts.quote: El dinosaurio fue descubierto en Lockesburg, Arkansas , y era un dinosaurio bípedo ornitomimosaurio.

facts.statement: The official scientific description of Arkansaurus was published on March 19, 2018, in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology by ReBecca Hunt-Foster and posthumously by James H. Quinn.
facts.quote: La descripción oficial de este dinosaurio fue publicada el 19 de marzo de 2018 en el Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology por los paleontólogos ReBecca Hunt-Foster y, póstumamente, por James H. Quinn.

facts.statement: Arkansaurus fossils exhibit unique anatomical features including differentiated toe bone bases, a laterally compressed ovoid third metatarsal, and a distal ungual phalanx with a very weak flexor tubercle, lacking spurs.
facts.quote: El estudio determinó que los fósiles contienen una combinación de detalles anatómicos únicos, tales como los huesos base de la uñas en el pie diferenciados diferenciadas, tercera metatarso lateralmente comprimido que es ovoide en vista proximal, y una falange ungueal distal con un muy débil tubérculo flexor, que carecen de espolones.

facts.statement: In 2018, Arkansaurus was placed within Ornithomimosauria in a basal position outside the Ornithomimidae family.
facts.quote: Arkansaurus se colocó en Ornithomimosauria en 2018, en una posición basal fuera de los Ornithomimidae.

facts.statement: As an ornithomimosaur, Arkansaurus is a rare representative of the Early Cretaceous group in North America, more closely related to Nedcolbertia than to contemporary Asian forms.
facts.quote: Como ornitomimosaurio, Arkansaurus sería un raro representante de ese grupo del Cretácico Inferior de América del Norte, más emparentado con Nedcolbertia que con las formas asiáticas contemporáneas.

facts.statement: Arkansaurus lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some researchers suspected the fossils were a forgery, but this hypothesis was quickly refuted by experts.
facts.quote: Por esta razón, expresó la sospecha de que era una falsificación, lo cual fue rápidamente contradicho por los expertos.

facts.statement: In 2002 and 2003, ReBecca Hunt-Foster suggested Arkansaurus might be a separate taxon related to Ornitholestes, but concluded the fossil remains did not justify its formal designation.
facts.quote: Esta última presentó trabajos en 2002 y 2003, en las que concluyó que probablemente era un taxón separado, posiblemente relacionado con Ornitholestes, pero que los restos no justificaban su designación.

facts.statement: ReBecca Hunt noted similarities between the Arkansaurus foot and footprints found in the Glen Rose Formation of Texas and the Moenave Formation of Utah.
facts.quote: Hunt señaló la semejanza del pie con las huellas encontradas en la Formación Glen Rose de Texas y la Formación Moenave de Utah.
